items.text: Oil prices (WTI -4.4%, Brent -5.9% WoW) have eased from recent highs, but ECB cited persistent energy shocks posing twin risks: upside to inflation and downside to growth. For credit investors, energy volatility remains a tail risk to refinancing capacity in leveraged energy names and working capital stress across industrials.

Headline CPI printed 3.72% YoY (up from 3.35%), core CPI 2.57% (up from 2.45%), and PPI jumped to 6.52% (from 6.29%). Stickiness is broadening: services prices rose 0.4% MoM in October, matching September, with prices paid in ISM Services remaining elevated at 73. Persistent core pressure keeps real rates higher for longer, extending stress on rate-sensitive credit.

Jobless claims rose to 200k (from 191k), unemployment held at 4.1%, and payrolls showed a large but irregular beat (+165k from +60k prior). Wage growth (AHE) has stalled at 3.12% YoY. Labor market is cooling but not cracking, constraining the Fed's room to cut, while wage disinflation remains elusive—a double squeeze on credit margins.

Fed funds held at 4.0%, 10Y UST jumped +29bp to 5.15%, and 2Y rose to 4.88%, steepening the curve from 0.32 to 0.29 (flattening slight). Markets price ~94% odds of ECB hike in December and 67bp of cuts over 12 months. Fed paused with sticky inflation—near-term easing is off the table; refinancing risk for high-yield and leveraged borrowers extends.

HY OAS compressed 7bp to 323, IG OAS tightened 1bp to 89, and CCC spreads improved 15bp to 1316. VIX fell 630bp to 19.3 from panic highs. Tightening reflects equity stabilization and energy relief, but is vulnerable to CPI/rate surprises ahead. Watch for deterioration if services inflation remains sticky and Fed stays restrictive.

Existing-home sales fell 5.5% in October, reaching their lowest level since August 2010, with inventory rose to 5.1 months of supply. Consumer sentiment bounced to 51.0 in November preliminary (from 48.0 final October), but this reflects equity stabilization noise rather than durable fundamentals. Housing credit: stress is acute and likely to persist given mortgage rates remain elevated.

GDPNow stands at 3.481% (up from 3.27%), supported by resilient services (ISM 54.5) and sticky inflation in goods. Retail sales consensus expects +0.2% MoM for October. Growth remains steady but increasingly uneven: services holding, housing crashing, manufacturing stalling in China (NBS PMI 49.3). Credit investors face divergence: late-cycle service-led growth masking structural weakness in housing and trade-exposed sectors.

themeCards.title: Housing collapse, inventory surge
themeCards.statusLine: Existing home sales dropped 5.5% MoM in October to their lowest level since August 2010. At 3.75 million annualized, they are currently running about 32% below 2016–17 levels and almost 40% below 2021 levels. The inventory of existing homes available for sale increased to 5.1 months' worth of sales, the highest since November 2015.
themeCards.relevance: Credit: Housing-dependent sectors (homebuilders, REITs, mortgage servicers) face negative equity. Broader impact on consumer wealth, spending, and regional bank credit quality. Mortgage lenders face margin compression and refinancing losses. Special situations: stressed housing finance, servicer dislocations, and high-LTV portfolio bleeds.

themeCards.title: Sticky core inflation, services pricing
themeCards.statusLine: Overall consumer prices rose 0.4% MoM in October and core prices rose 0.3%, each topping expectations by a tenth. There was a sharp 0.5% MoM jump in food prices. Both goods and services prices rose 0.4% MoM, the latter matching the September read and pointing to more sustained and broader price pressures in the services space.
themeCards.relevance: Keeps real rates higher for longer, constraining refinancing and hurting fixed-rate credit. Services pricing (73.0 ISM) shows margin resilience but signals labor cost pass-through. Credit investors: duration risk, curve steepening, and IG spreads compressed on false hope of imminent cuts. Expect volatility if core PCE remains above 3% through year-end.

themeCards.title: China manufacturing contraction risk
themeCards.statusLine: China's manufacturing activity returns to contraction in October after a brief improvement, with its purchasing managers' index falling to 49.3 and new export orders weakening, intensifying concerns over domestic demand and deflation. Export orders fell to 48.7, reversing September's recovery.
themeCards.relevance: Spillover to global manufacturing, industrials credit, and emerging-market refinancing. US export-sensitive sectors (cyclicals, tech supply chains) face demand headwinds. Special situations: watch for China credit stress contagion via commodity and capital goods defaults; EM sovereign and corporate refinancing widening under growth slowdown.

themeCards.title: ECB hiking cycle extension uncertainty
themeCards.statusLine: The ECB held its key rates steady on 2026-10-29, keeping the deposit rate at 2.50% as an energy shock clouds the outlook. Energy prices have continued to climb, creating upside risks for inflation and downside risks for growth. Markets now price 94% odds of a December hike despite growth concerns.
themeCards.relevance: Divergence between Fed pausing and ECB potentially tightening further widdles DXI, stresses EZ corporates (esp. high-debt names), and triggers currency translation losses for US multinationals with EZ exposure. IG spreads in EUR and cross-currency basis widen. Credit investors: monitor EZ HY spreads and subordinated debt; default risk rises if growth slips while rates stay elevated.

themeCards.title: Steep curve, long-end rally exhaustion
themeCards.statusLine: 10Y UST jumped +29bp WoW to 5.15%, 2Y rose to 4.88%, curve slightly flattening (10-2 spread now 0.29 vs 0.32). Long-end underperformance signals growing concern about terminal rates, fiscal risks, and inflation persistence. Curve is steeper than typical late-cycle yet not inverted—a signal of deceleration without recession pricing.
themeCards.relevance: Refinancing wall for maturities beyond 5Y becomes acute; borrowers who rolled forward in 2024–2025 face substantial wall. Curve steepness favors floating-rate paper but pressures fixed-rate refinancing costs. Special situations: watch for covenant tests, leverage tests, and capex cuts in investment-grade names with large 2027–2028 maturity spikes.

themeCards.title: Labor market cooling, wage disinflation stalling
themeCards.statusLine: Claims rose to 200k WoW (from 191k), unemployment held steady at 4.1%, but AHE is stuck at 3.12% YoY and flattening. Payrolls beat (165k) looks outsized after prior miss (60k) and likely reflects seasonality noise. Labor market is cooling but wage pressure refuses to break, constraining the Fed's willingness to cut.
themeCards.relevance: Prolonged labor cost pressure keeps services margins resilient near-term but erodes leverage in cost-conscious sectors. Unemployment uptick potential near 4.5% would trigger spread widening. Credit investors: watch for covenant leverage tests in labor-heavy services names; restructuring candidates emerging in retail, hospitality, leisure where margin compression meets debt walls.

ecb.delta: Unchanged since 2026-09-16; markets price 94% odds of +25bp hike Dec 17

chinaPMI.delta: October NBS reading; below 50 = contraction; exports weak at 48.7

ismServices.delta: October 2026; miss forecast of 54.8; new orders fell 3.9 pts; prices stuck at 73

existingHome.delta: October SAAR; down 5.5% MoM, down 8.8% YoY; lowest since Aug 2010

consensus.CPI: 3.4% YoY expected (Oct actual ~4.0–4.1% per Haver/Econvitals estimates)
consensus.PCE: Est. 3.2–3.3% core YoY (via Oct PPI/CPI decomposition; exact PCE pending release)
consensus.ISM Mfg: 55.5 expected (Oct actual ~55.5; Nov data due Dec 2)
consensus.ISM Services: 54.8 expected (Oct actual 54.5; Nov data due Dec 3)

regime.label: Late-cycle with energy shock
regime.detail: Sticky core inflation, housing collapse, labor cooling but wages stuck, curve steepening, credit spreads tight despite growth divergence—Fed paused, ECB likely tightens; refinancing wall extends, real rates stay elevated.
